subject: Is it possible to create Johnson-Neman plots for second order SEMs with results obtained using the lavaan package?

messages.author: f0252592a5d0339c
messages.subject: Is it possible to create Johnson-Neman plots for second order SEMs with results obtained using the lavaan package?
parts:
I'm trying to plot a J-N diagram with the results of my SEM where I test a moderation effect (latent moderator, first order construct) between an independent variable (categorical variable, 2 values) on a latent dependent variable (second order construct).

Now I want to do two things:

1.) I want to visualize simple slopes (this I achieve trough jeremy dawsons 2-way interaction excel or R packages). This is something I succeeded in.

2.) I would like to assess the conditions under which the effect of the independent variable on the dependent variable becomes significant through the  moderator variable. And THIS is what eludes me. I tried several methods, But I don't seem to understand how you can model a complex latent SEM and use for example the Johnson_Neyman() function in the interaction package for R.

Moreover, I read this article (Lin, 2020, https://doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2020.1732826) and this one (Schoemann & Jorgensen, 2021, https://doi.org/10.3390/psych3030024) and the takeaways seem to be that

1.) there is no real method yet (at least not in R) 
AND
2.) that this endeavor is not fruitful, because "the J-N technique is of limited value. The scale of latent variables is arbitrary, and determining the specific values of the latent moderator where the simple slope is different from zero is not as useful as identifying how simple slopes change across values of the moderator, which can be accomplished using a simple slopes approach." (Schoemann & Jorgensen, 2021, p.332).

My question is the: should I let go and don't fuss abut J-N plots or is there some sort of work around for that?
